dedupe_keys.name: gnss scintillation data from more than 40 arctic receivers for the geomagnetic storm of may 2024

description: This dataset, published by Knut Stanley Jacobsen of the Norwegian Mapping Authority with colleagues from the Technical University of Denmark, the Finnish Meteorological Institute and the University of New Brunswick, gathers data from more than 40 ground-based GNSS scintillation receivers across the Arctic in Finland, Norway, Greenland and Canada during the major geomagnetic storm of May 2024, the strongest in two decades. The files hold many scintillation parameters (amplitude and phase indices and related quantities) together with all the metadata needed to use them, in the Biscintillation Exchange Format (BiScEF), an HDF5 and netCDF4 layout with a format description and scripts maintained on GitHub by Kartverket. Coverage: Arctic and sub-Arctic stations in four countries during the May 2024 storm. Format and access: a ZIP of HDF5 and netCDF4 files (about 0.87 GB) with a receiver map and format description, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one event; receivers of different types and operators; indices describe signal fluctuation, not receiver outages. Simulation uses: event-based scenarios of GNSS degradation during extreme space weather for resilience studies of positioning and timing used by transport, power and telecom. Related records: the University of Bergen Svalbard collection gives long-term Arctic scintillation series; NOAA SWPC products and the GFZ Kp index describe the storm drivers.
